bull_bear.body:
- The deck's headline capital-efficiency metric is annualised standalone ROIC, shown rising from 8.86% in FY16 to 23.72% in FY26, having been negative in FY21 (-5.39%) and FY22 (-4.01%) before recovering from 0.39% in FY23 to 14.02% in FY24 and 17.81% in FY25.
- Invested capital is shown expanding over the same window, from ₹1,493 Cr in FY16 to ₹4,091 Cr in FY26 — with the step-up concentrated in FY26 (₹2,843 Cr in FY25).
- Operating PAT on the same slide moves from ₹132 Cr in FY16 through negative years in FY21 (-₹128 Cr) and FY22 (-₹108 Cr) to ₹971 Cr in FY26.
- The deck discloses no dividend, debt, or shareholder-return policy.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body:
- On its Light Commercial Vehicle platform the deck claims "Market leader in the segment with over 70% market share", alongside "India's most preferred Ambulance maker" and "Fastest growing School Bus Manufacturer".
- Stated vision is "To be one of the world's most preferred providers of shared passenger mobility solutions and rank among the top ten van manufacturers globally", with the goal of "safe, sustainable and reliable shared passenger mobility solutions".
- Defence linkage is claimed as a differentiator: "All Bofors Guns at our borders are powered by the Mercedes licensed OM 616 engine made by Force Motors" and "The Light Strike Vehicles inducted by the Indian Army to conduct surgical strikes are built on Force Gurkha platform".
- The German OEM franchise is exclusive-sounding in the deck's own words: dedicated plants manufacture engines and cooling modules "for all BMW cars and SUVs made in India" and engines and axles "for all Mercedes-Benz cars and SUVs made in India".
- Lineage is presented as a moat: founded 1958, carrying forward Shri N.K. Firodia's legacy, having coined the term autorickshaw and introduced the three-wheeler Tempo in 1948, which "became synonymous with light commercial vehicles in India".
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Group structure] Force Motors sits within the Dr. Abhay Firodia Group of Companies, stated as having "Enterprise value exceeding ₹46,000 crores"; the chart shows 99.88% and 61.5% against Jaya Hind Industries Pvt Ltd and Force Motors Limited respectively, with the note "Please note % represent promoter holding".
- [Joint venture] Force MTU Power Systems Pvt Ltd is "a joint venture between Force Motors (51%) and Rolls-Royce Power Systems AG (49%)"; separately, Jaya Hind Industries holds 100% of LMG Manufacturing GmbH, Germany, which it acquired.
- [HR transformation] "Force Motors launched Project Lakshya, a strategic HR transformation initiative designed to create a digitally empowered, agile, and leadership-driven organisation", spanning learning & development, employee engagement, digital capability building and culture shift; the company "partnered with SP Jain School of Global Management to launch Executive and Advanced Leadership Programmes for high-potential employees".
- [Quality accreditation] "All Force Motors plants are certified by TUV for ISO, EMS, IATF and NABL" (ISO 9001, IATF 16949, ISO 14001, ISO 45001), and the Material Testing Laboratory and Standards Room are NABL-certified.
- [Tax regime change] The deck footnotes twice that "During FY'26 (from Q2) Company has shifted to new tax regime", which affects comparability of the PAT series.
business.title: Notable from the deck

deepdive.thesis: The deck positions Force Motors as a Pune-headquartered vehicle maker built on "Over Six Decades Of Indo-German Collaboration" — a dominant light commercial vehicle/van franchise (Traveller, Urbania, Trax, Gurkha) paired with a high-tech aggregate business assembling engines and axles for BMW and Mercedes-Benz in India and Series 1600 MTU engines through a Rolls-Royce Power Systems joint venture.
